findings.text: the renamed arm is quoted as "44 failed, 17,393 passed, 184 skipped, 1 xfailed in 25:38", but its cited log logs/after-suite-v2.log ends "44 failed, 17393 passed, 184 skipped, 1136 deselected, 48 warnings in 1538.78s (0:25:38)" and carries no xfailed anywhere, so the landing record states a number its own log does not report.

the origin/document_label guard added in this diff has no test that makes either violation fire: deleting the whole loop leaves the 18-test gate green, because test_cutover_reports_a_surface_the_document_does_not_carry asserts the tool does not judge labels.

the counts-unreconciled violation is never made to fire by the suite; test_check_reconciles_hits_kept_protected_and_leftover only asserts it stays silent, so a regression that stops appending the violation keeps the record's "a search that loses or double-counts a hit fails" claim green and unproven.

test_cutover_reports_a_surface_the_document_does_not_carry sets a row's label to "Invented surface" and then asserts check_cutover(path).ok, so the test's name claims a refusal the assertion certifies is absent; it documents the gap but contributes no guard.

the row count is asserted as len(claimed_inventory) + len(claimed_brief) + 1, where the literal 1 encodes exactly one duplicated document label (registry and azure both claim "Registry images"); splitting that label or adding a second shared one reddens a correct edit.
